I was travelling alone in Amsterdam and bought magic truffles at a smart shop, the guy said one bag was a normal dose. I ate them in my hotel room in the late afternoon. The room was tiny, with no window, just a skylight. As the truffles kicked in, the room started to shrink. The walls were moving inward and the ceiling was coming down. I became convinced the hotel was a trap, that the staff had drugged me on purpose and were going to come in and take my organs or something. I could hear footsteps in the hallway and voices in a language I didn't understand and every sound was them coming for me.

I pushed the desk and the chair against the door. I called reception and told them I knew what they were doing and that I'd call the police. The woman at reception was very confused and said she would send someone up to check on me, which of course was exactly what I was afraid of. When someone knocked I hid in the shower and turned on the water so I wouldn't hear them. They went away. I stayed in the shower for what must have been two hours, the water running cold. I kept looking up at the skylight and seeing faces looking down.

At some point I called my sister back home. It was the middle of the night there. She talked me through it for an hour, telling me that I'd taken drugs and that this would pass. I didn't really believe her but her voice helped. By morning I was exhausted and ashamed. I checked out early and the receptionist gave me a strange look.

Ich war mit zwei Freunden auf Pilzen in den Bergen, als plötzlich ein Gewitter aufzog. Die Blitze schlugen ganz in der Nähe ein, und ich hatte das Gefühl, dass Gott zornig auf uns ist und uns bestrafen will. Wir haben uns unter einen Felsvorsprung gekauert, und ich war mir sicher, dass wir sterben. Ich habe gebetet, obwohl ich gar nicht gläubig bin. Als das Gewitter vorbei war, schien die Sonne, und ich habe vor Erleichterung geweint.

I went to a psilocybin retreat in Portugal with the intention of working on anxiety that I'd had since the birth of my daughter two years earlier. The birth had been traumatic: an emergency C-section, I lost a lot of blood, and for several minutes nobody told me whether my baby was alive. I'd talked about it in therapy, but I still had anxiety, and I hoped the retreat would help me process it.

The retreat included breathwork before the ceremony, which I now think was a bad combination for me. When the psilocybin came on, I was lying on a mat with an eyeshade, and suddenly I was back on the operating table. I could feel the tugging in my belly, the cold, the numbness from the spinal block. I could hear the beeping of the machines and the surgeon's voice. And then the silence where my baby's cry should have been.

But this time it went further. In the trip, the baby didn't cry. I saw her being carried away, grey and still, and I knew she was dead. I knew with total certainty that my daughter had died at birth and that the last two years had been a dream, a fantasy my mind had made up to protect me. I screamed and screamed. I was trying to get off the mat to find her. I was bleeding, in my mind. I could feel the warm blood soaking the sheets.

The facilitators held me down because I was trying to run, and that made it even more like the operating table, being held down, helpless. I kept shouting my daughter's name. One facilitator tried to tell me my daughter was at home with my husband, safe, and I didn't believe her. I thought she was one of the nurses lying to me.

I dissolved after that. I was the birth, the blood, the operating table, the silence. There wasn't a me anymore, just this huge grief.

It went on for hours. Towards the end, they let me call my husband on video and I saw my daughter, sleepy, in her pyjamas, waving at the screen. I couldn't stop crying. Even then, part of me was saying 'that's a video, that's not her'.
Took acid with my brother. He was fine, but I suddenly became convinced I had killed someone earlier that day and forgotten. Total paranoia, checking the news, checking my hands for blood.

Wir waren auf einer Exkursion mit der Uni und hatten am letzten Abend zu dritt LSD genommen. Wir dachten, die Wirkung wäre am nächsten Morgen vorbei, aber ich hatte offenbar eine sehr starke Pappe erwischt. Am Morgen mussten wir mit dem Zug zurückfahren, und ich war immer noch voll drauf.

Im Zug wurde es schlimm. Der Wagen war voll, und ich hatte das Gefühl, dass alle mich anstarren. Dann kam der Schaffner, und ich konnte meine Fahrkarte nicht finden, obwohl sie in meiner Hand war. Ich habe sie nicht erkannt. Der Schaffner wurde ungeduldig und lauter, und ich bekam eine Panikattacke. Mein Herz raste, ich bekam keine Luft, und ich war mir sicher, dass er mich verhaften wird und dass alle wissen, dass ich Drogen genommen habe. Meine Kommilitonen versuchten, mir zu helfen, aber die waren selbst noch nicht ganz klar.

Beim nächsten Halt bin ich einfach ausgestiegen, ohne Gepäck, in einer Stadt, die ich nicht kannte. Ich bin stundenlang durch die Straßen gelaufen und hatte das Gefühl, dass die Häuser auf mich herabschauen. Ich wusste nicht mehr, wie ich nach Hause kommen soll, und hatte panische Angst, dass ich nie wieder normal werde. Irgendwann habe ich mich auf eine Bank am Bahnhof gesetzt und gewartet, bis es vorbeigeht. Am Abend hat mich mein Vater abgeholt. Ich habe ihm gesagt, dass ich einen Kreislaufzusammenbruch hatte.

I did ketamine and mushrooms at home alone. I was going through a breakup and wanted to escape. I took too much ketamine and went into what people call a k-hole. I left my body and was floating above it, looking down at myself on the couch, and I couldn't get back in. Then I wasn't even floating anymore, there was no 'I'. I was spread out across some kind of grid that went on forever. I was terrified that my body had died and I was stuck as this formless awareness. When I came back I couldn't move my legs properly for a while, and I lay there crying for hours, feeling like I wasn't really back, like only part of me had returned.

It was the day of a major terrorist attack in another country. I didn't know that when I took the LSD with two friends at my flat in the morning. We were planning a chilled day with films and music.

Around noon, one of my friends got a news alert on his phone and turned on the TV. They were showing live footage, the smoke, the sirens, people running. The commentators were talking about multiple attacks and possible further targets. I was at the peak. I'd never seen anything like that while on a psychedelic.

I became completely convinced that a world war had started. That this was the beginning of the end, and that within hours there would be attacks everywhere, including our city. The images on the screen were coming out of the TV and filling the room. I could smell smoke. Every siren outside sounded like the next attack. I told my friends we had to get to a basement. They were scared too but less than me. One of them tried to turn the TV off and I shouted at him not to, because we needed to know what was happening.

Then I started hearing planes overhead. I don't know if they were real. I was sure they were bombers. I went down to the building's basement, which was dark and smelled of mould, and I sat there among the bicycles for maybe three hours. My friends came down and tried to get me back up. I didn't want to leave.

While I was in the basement I lost track of who I was. I felt like all the victims at once, I felt the explosions, I felt bodies being torn apart. I felt that I was dying in a thousand places simultaneously. I was crying and shaking and repeating 'I'm sorry, I'm sorry'.

My mother called around 5pm. She was worried because of the news and because I hadn't been answering my phone. One of my friends answered and told her I was 'not feeling well'. She insisted on speaking to me. When I heard her voice I broke down completely and told her I loved her and that I was sorry I'd never been a good son, because I thought we were all going to die. She was very frightened. She drove over.

By the time she arrived the LSD was wearing off and I was beginning to understand that the attack was terrible but not a world war. I was so ashamed. My mother stayed the night. I couldn't watch the news for weeks.

Ayahuasca in einer kleinen Gruppe in der Schweiz. Ich habe mich ständig übergeben und dabei Schlangen gesehen, die aus meinem Mund kamen. Ich konnte nicht mehr unterscheiden, was echt ist. Ich hatte Angst, dass ich mich selbst auskotze, meine Organe, mein Ich. Die Leiterin war ruhig und hat mich begleitet, trotzdem war es die schlimmste Nacht meines Lebens.

A friend obtained synthetic mescaline and we took it at his house in the countryside. Nobody told us how long it lasts. The come-up was slow, two hours of nausea and restlessness. Then it hit hard and just kept going. Hour after hour. By the 10th hour I was desperate for it to end and it didn't. The sun went down and came back up, or at least I thought it did, and I was still tripping.

Somewhere in the night I became delirious. I couldn't tell what time it was or how long I'd been there. I had conversations with people who weren't in the room. I thought I was in a hospital and that the doctors were keeping me in this state on purpose. I couldn't sleep, though I was beyond exhausted. My body felt like it was buzzing with electricity and my jaw ached from clenching.

By the 14th hour I started believing that it would never end, that I had permanently altered my brain chemistry and that I'd be like this for the rest of my life. That was the worst fear. My friend was in a similar state and couldn't help me. I finally slept a little the next afternoon, and when I woke up the world still looked wrong for several more days.

I have a family history of schizophrenia, my uncle. I knew it was risky but I was 19 and felt invincible. I took a moderate dose of LSD at a friend's place. A couple of hours in, I started to hear voices. Not the usual auditory distortions, but distinct voices, talking about me in the third person, commenting on what I was doing. They were critical and nasty. I realised what was happening and that made me panic, I was sure I'd triggered the same illness as my uncle. The voices got louder and started arguing with each other about whether I deserved to live. I covered my ears and rocked back and forth on the floor.
Pilze, viel Angst, Gefühl zu sterben. Meine Freunde haben mich zum Glück beruhigt.

I was 17 and had a house party at my parents' place while they were away for the weekend. A friend brought LSD and five of us took it. It was the first time for all of us. It was fun for a while, then the doorbell rang and it was my parents, who'd come home a day early because my grandmother was sick. They walked into a house full of drunk and tripping teenagers. My dad was furious and started shouting. To me his face became a monster's face, red and huge. My mum was crying. I couldn't explain anything, I couldn't even talk properly. They sent everyone home and I had to sit at the kitchen table while they interrogated me. I was terrified and felt like I was being judged by the whole universe. I thought they'd disown me. My dad found the remaining tabs in my room and called a friend's parents and it all became a huge drama. I spent the night in my room hearing them argue downstairs and seeing the walls bleed.
